title: Jamaican Curried Beef Patties in Flaky Turmeric Pastry
summary: A buttery pastry coloured with turmeric and curry powder is chilled, rolled and cut into rounds, then filled with beef mince simmered with onion, spring onion, Scotch bonnet, thyme, allspice and curry and thickened with breadcrumbs, crimped into half-moons and baked until golden.
equipment: 2 baking trays lined with baking paper

ingredients.item: plain flour, plus extra for rolling
fine sea salt or table salt
cold unsalted butter, cut into 1 cm cubes
ice-cold water, plus 1-2 tbsp if needed
Scotch bonnet chilli, seeded and finely chopped
ingredients.note: use less for a milder filling

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Make the pastry
steps.text: Rub cold butter into the spiced flour, bind with egg and ice-cold water, and chill at least 1 hour.

steps.title: Cook the filling
steps.text: Soften the onion, spring onion, garlic and chilli, then brown the beef and add the spices.

steps.title: Thicken
steps.text: Simmer with breadcrumbs and water until thick and the beef reaches 71 °C, then cool completely.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Roll the pastry thin, cut 15 cm rounds, fill, fold and crimp with a fork.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Glaze with egg and bake until golden and the filling reads 74 °C.

tips: Keep the butter and water very cold for a flaky crust.
Cool the filling fully before shaping, or the pastry will soften and tear.
Turmeric stains; roll the dough on baking paper if your worktop is porous.
storage: Refrigerate baked patties within 2 hours for up to 3 days and reheat in the oven until piping hot. Freeze unbaked patties up to 1 month and bake from frozen, adding 10-15 minutes.
